correctness.rationale: Checked analytically and independently exhaustively within the bounded needed lattice-vector norm range: in L0=2Z^3 union ((1,1,1)+2Z^3) there are precisely six nonzero vectors ±2ei of l1 length 2 and eight odd sign vectors of l1 length 3; no other vector has length <=3. For r<=1 interiors do not overlap. For 1<=r<=3/2 only differences ±2ei create positive-volume pair lenses; centered at coordinate x1=1+t each lens section is a planar l1 ball of radius r-1-|t| and volume integral ∫_{-(r-1)}^(r-1)2(r-1-|t|)^2dt=(4/3)(r-1)^3. Three unordered short pairs per volume-4 lattice fundamental cell yield exact double-covered fraction (r-1)^3. Distinct short neighbors differ by l1 distance 4>2r, forbidding any positive-volume triple intersection. Inclusion/exclusion gives covered=r^3/3-(r-1)^3, uncovered=1-r^3/3+(r-1)^3=r(3-r)(3-2r)/3 and singles=r^3/3-2(r-1)^3. At r=3/2 uncovered0, double1/8 and single7/8, with exact near-threshold polynomial 3epsilon/2-2epsilon^3/3. These are symbolic infinite periodic consequences of a proven bounded neighbor classification, not numerical sampling.
